work: Enarratio in Epistolam B. Pauli ad Colossenses
source: Dionysii Cartusiani Opera Omnia, t. XIII (Montreuil)

2.title: ELUCIDATIO CAPITULI SECUNDI : VOLO ENIM VOS SCIRE QUALEM SOLLICITUDINEM HABEAM PRO VOBIS.
2.title_en: Elucidation of the second chapter: For I would have you know what manner of care I have for you.

paras.t: Cœptam in præcedenti capitulo exhortationem de vitandis cærimonialibus legis, prosequitur Apostolus in isto capitulo, admonens Colossenses ut falsos ac simulatos vitent doctores. Et ut sibi acquiescant facilius, manifestat quantum de eorum salute sollicitetur. Volo enim vos scire, ut amanti credatis, qualem sollicitudinem habeam pro vobis, et pro his qui sunt Laodiciæ (quæ est civitas Asiæ), id est pro vestra Laodicensiumque salute, ne ab impostoribus fallamini, a quibus præventi jam estis, et quicumque non viderunt faciem meam in carne, id est pro ceteris universis fidelibus quibus ipse in propria persona non prædicavi neque apparui. Ut consolentur corda ipsorum, id est, ob hoc sollicitus sum, quatenus corda ipsorum consolationem recipiant ex allocutione mea per epistolas, quæ consolata non sunt ex præsentia et immediata prædicatione mea; et sitis instructi, id est prudenter exercitati, in caritate, id est in actibus dilectionis Dei et proximi; vel, Instructi in caritate, id est de caritate Christi ad nos, ut sciatis et consideretis quantum Christus dilexerit nos, qui ait: Majorem hac dilectionem nemo habet, quam ut animam suam ponat quis pro amicis suis. Sitis quoque instructi, seu per caritatis instructionem tendentes, et in omnes divitias plenitudinis intellectus, id est perfectissimos habitus intellectuales, ut impleamini donis sapientiæ et intellectus, consilii atque scientiæ, in agnitionem mysterii, id est ad hoc ut actualiter consideretis mysterium, id est sacrum secretum, Dei Patris et Domini nostri Jesu Christi: per quod intelligi potest unitas Patris et Filii in essentia, et distinctio in persona; vel ipsa incarnatio, quæ est mysterium Patris tanquam auctoris, et Christi tanquam assumptoris vel exsecutoris.
paras.en: The exhortation begun in the preceding chapter about avoiding the ceremonies of the law the Apostle pursues in this chapter, warning the Colossians to shun false and feigned teachers. And so that they may the more readily heed him, he shows how anxious he is for their salvation. [[2:1|For I would have you know|Volo enim vos scire]], so that you may believe one who loves you, [[2:1|what manner of care I have for you and for them that are at Laodicea|qualem sollicitudinem habeam pro vobis, et pro his qui sunt Laodiciæ]] (which is a city of Asia), that is, for your salvation and that of the Laodiceans, lest you be deceived by impostors, by whom you have already been forestalled, [[2:1|and whosoever have not seen my face in the flesh|et quicumque non viderunt faciem meam in carne]], that is, for all the other faithful to whom I have not preached nor appeared in my own person. [[2:2|That their hearts may be comforted|Ut consolentur corda ipsorum]]: that is, I am anxious for this, that their hearts, which have not been comforted by my presence and my preaching in person, may receive comfort from my addressing them by letters; and that you may be [[2:2|instructed|instructi]], that is, prudently exercised, [[2:2|in charity|in caritate]], that is, in acts of love of God and of neighbour; or, Instructed in charity, that is, about the charity of Christ towards us, so that you may know and consider how much Christ has loved us, who says: [[John 15:13|Greater love than this no man hath, that a man lay down his life for his friends|Majorem hac dilectionem nemo habet, quam ut animam suam ponat quis pro amicis suis]]. May you also be instructed, or tending through the instruction of charity, [[2:2|and unto all riches of fulness of understanding|et in omnes divitias plenitudinis intellectus]], that is, unto the most perfect intellectual habits, so that you may be filled with the gifts of wisdom and understanding, of counsel and knowledge[[Is 11:2||]], [[2:2|unto the knowledge of the mystery|in agnitionem mysterii]], that is, to this end, that you may actually consider the mystery, that is, the sacred secret, [[2:2|of God the Father and of Christ Jesus|Dei Patris et Domini nostri Jesu Christi]]: by which may be understood the unity of the Father and the Son in essence and their distinction in person; or the incarnation itself, which is the mystery of the Father as its author, and of Christ as the one who assumed [our nature] and carried it out.

paras.t: In quo Christo sunt omnes thesauri, id est copiosissima plenitudo, sapientiæ divinorum et scientiæ creaturarum absconditi, id est incomprehensibiliter exsistentes. Christus namque secundum divinitatem, est ipsa æterna atque immensa sapientia, cujus non est numerus, estque increata scientia: cui convenit illud, O altitudo divitiarum sapientiæ et scientiæ Dei! Secundum humanitatem quoque assumptam, repletus est sapientia in contemplatione divinorum, et scientia in speculatione creaturarum, præsertim quum anima Christi præ universis Beatis, Divinitatem ac Trinitatem ab exordio suæ creationis clarius vidit, et omnia illa cognoscit quæ cognoscit et Verbum, scientia visionis, id est cuncta quæ unquam fuerunt, sunt aut erunt.
paras.en: [[2:3|In whom|In quo]], in Christ, [[2:3|are hid all the treasures|sunt omnes thesauri]], that is, the most abundant fulness, [[2:3|of wisdom|sapientiæ]] of divine things [[2:3|and knowledge|et scientiæ]] of creatures, [[2:3|hid|absconditi]], that is, existing incomprehensibly. For Christ according to His divinity is that eternal and immense wisdom of which there is no number[[Ps 146:5||]], and is uncreated knowledge, to whom applies that word: [[Rom 11:33|O the depth of the riches of the wisdom and of the knowledge of God!|O altitudo divitiarum sapientiæ et scientiæ Dei!]]! According to the humanity He assumed, too, He is filled with wisdom in contemplating divine things and with knowledge in considering creatures, above all since the soul of Christ, beyond all the Blessed, saw the Godhead and the Trinity more clearly from the first moment of its creation, and knows all that the Word knows by the knowledge of vision [that is, knowledge of what actually exists at any time, as distinct from the merely possible], that is, all things that ever were, are, or will be.

paras.t: Hoc autem dico, ut nemo vos decipiat, id est, fidei vestræ simplicitatem inficiat, in sublimitate sermonis, id est per verba profunda secundum apparentiam, et fucata seu subtilia argumenta. Denique ista admoneo: Nam etsi corpore absum a vobis, id est a vobis distans loco ac corporali separatione, sed spiritu, id est mentis consideratione, vobiscum sum, tum quia de vobis sæpius cogito, tum quia in spiritu prophetico quasi præsens inspicio quid agatis: quemadmodum Eliseus præsens fuit quando Giezi accepit munera Naaman; gaudens in Domino de vestro profectu, et videns, id est cognoscens, ordinem vestrum, id est vitæ vestræ ordinationem, quomodo omnia honeste et secundum ordinem fiunt in vobis, et firmamentum ejus quæ in Christo est fidei vestræ, id est stabilitatem seu robur fidei vestræ quam in Christo habetis.
paras.en: [[2:4|Now this I say, that no man may deceive you|Hoc autem dico, ut nemo vos decipiat]], that is, corrupt the simplicity of your faith, [[2:4|by loftiness of words|in sublimitate sermonis]], that is, by words profound in appearance and by specious or subtle arguments. Moreover I give this warning: [[2:5|For though I be absent in body|Nam etsi corpore absum]] from you, that is, distant from you in place and bodily separation, [[2:5|yet in spirit|sed spiritu]], that is, in the regard of my mind, [[2:5|I am with you|vobiscum sum]], both because I often think of you, and because in the prophetic spirit I see, as if present, what you are doing: just as Eliseus was present when Giezi took the gifts of Naaman[[4 Kings 5:1||]]; [[2:5|rejoicing|gaudens]] in the Lord at your progress, [[2:5|and beholding|et videns]], that is, knowing, [[2:5|your order|ordinem vestrum]], that is, the ordering of your life, how all things are done among you decently and according to order[[1 Cor 14:40||]], [[2:5|and the steadfastness of your faith which is in Christ|et firmamentum ejus quæ in Christo est fidei vestræ]], that is, the stability or strength of the faith that you have in Christ.

paras.t: Consequenter hortatur eos ad perseverantiam ac profectum in bonis. Sicut ergo accepistis Christum Jesum Dominum nostrum, id est, sicut credendo cœpistis conversari in Christo, in ipso ambulate, id est, sic exinde in eo procedite, proficiendo semper in melius, per imitationem vestigiorum Salvatoris. Sola namque perseverantia coronatur. Radicati, id est firmiter fixi, per modum radicis terræ inhærentis, et superædificati in ipso, id est in doctrina et gratia Christi, ita ut sitis domus seu habitaculum Dei, cujus fundamentum sit Christus seu doctrina et gratia ejus. Unde Ephesiis dictum est: Superædificati super fundamentum Apostolorum et Prophetarum. Et confirmati in fide, ut nec philosophicis rationibus, nec sensuum apparentiis, nec persecutionibus, recedatis a fidei sinceritate, sicut et didicistis ab Archippo ambulandum esse et standum in fide, qua nutante, tota virtutum structura vacillat, abundantes in illo in gratiarum actione, id est Deo copiose grates referendo.
paras.en: Next he exhorts them to perseverance and progress in good. [[2:6|As therefore you have received Jesus Christ the Lord|Sicut ergo accepistis Christum Jesum Dominum nostrum]], that is, as by believing you began to live in Christ, [[2:6|walk ye in him|in ipso ambulate]], that is, so henceforth go forward in Him, ever advancing to better, by following in the footsteps of the Saviour. For perseverance alone is crowned[[Matt 10:22||]]. [[2:7|Rooted|Radicati]], that is, firmly fixed, like a root clinging to the earth, [[2:7|and built up in him|et superædificati in ipso]], that is, in the doctrine and grace of Christ, so that you may be a house or dwelling of God whose foundation is Christ, or His doctrine and grace. Hence it was said to the Ephesians: [[Eph 2:20|Built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets|Superædificati super fundamentum Apostolorum et Prophetarum]]. [[2:7|And confirmed in the faith|Et confirmati in fide]], so that neither by philosophical reasonings, nor by the appearances of the senses, nor by persecutions, you depart from the purity of the faith, [[2:7|as also you have learned|sicut et didicistis]] from Archippus, that one must walk and stand in the faith, for if it totters the whole structure of the virtues shakes; [[2:7|abounding in him in thanksgiving|abundantes in illo in gratiarum actione]], that is, giving thanks to God abundantly.

paras.t: Advertendum autem, quod triplici via conabantur perversi hos Colossenses subvertere, scilicet, per philosophiam, per legis allegationem, per simulatam sanctitatem. Hos processus Apostolus reprobat. Videte ne quis vos decipiat per philosophiam, id est scientiam naturalem, studio philosophorum inventam, et inanem fallaciam, id est per argumenta sophistica, quæ videntur aliquid probare, sed non probant veraciter: philosophiam, inquam, procedentem ac judicantem secundum traditionem hominum, id est humanæ rationis discursum, secundum elementa hujus mundi, id est juxta ea quæ naturaliter apparent in rebus, videlicet secundum causas naturales et elementares, et solitum cursum rerum, et non secundum Christum: id est, deceptores isti atque philosophi, non secundum Christi doctrinam procedunt, considerando divinæ virtutis illimitatam potentiam, non determinatam ad naturalem ac solitum cursum seu ordinem rerum, sed supernaturalia et nobis incomprehensibilia operari valentem. In quo declaratur philosophorum fatuitas, asserentium Deum non posse aliquid agere præter naturalem ordinem rerum, et ultra humanæ rationis capacitatem. Propter quod negabant quidquid rationem excedit, videlicet Deum incarnatum, virginem peperisse, etc. — Cur autem his qui non procedunt secundum Christum, debeat contradici, subjungitur: quia in ipso, id est in Christi humana natura quasi in templo, habitat omnis plenitudo divinitatis, id est perfecta veraque divinitas cum omni sua perfectione. Personaliter enim in Christo unitæ sunt natura divina et humana. Habitat autem in ea corporaliter, id est, corpori ejus vere ac immediate conjuncta est, sicut et animæ ejus, non quod ipsa sit corpus. Porro divinitas dicitur sic unita, quoniam persona Verbi, quæ est divinitas, humanitati conjuncta est.
paras.en: Now note that the perverse were trying to subvert these Colossians in three ways: by philosophy, by appeal to the law, and by feigned holiness. These approaches the Apostle condemns. [[2:8|Beware lest any man cheat you by philosophy|Videte ne quis vos decipiat per philosophiam]], that is, natural science, discovered by the study of the philosophers, [[2:8|and vain deceit|et inanem fallaciam]], that is, by sophistical arguments, which seem to prove something but do not truly prove it: philosophy, I say, proceeding and judging [[2:8|according to the tradition of men|secundum traditionem hominum]], that is, the reasoning of human understanding, [[2:8|according to the elements of the world|secundum elementa hujus mundi]], that is, according to what appears naturally in things, namely according to natural and elementary causes and the usual course of things, [[2:8|and not according to Christ|et non secundum Christum]]: that is, these deceivers and philosophers do not proceed according to the doctrine of Christ, by considering the unlimited might of the divine power, which is not bound to the natural and usual course or order of things, but is able to work things supernatural and incomprehensible to us. In this is shown the folly of the philosophers who assert that God cannot do anything beyond the natural order of things and beyond the capacity of human reason. For this reason they denied whatever exceeds reason, namely that God became incarnate, that a virgin gave birth, and so on. — Why those who do not proceed according to Christ ought to be opposed is added: [[2:9|For in him|quia in ipso]], that is, in Christ's human nature as in a temple, [[2:9|dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead|habitat omnis plenitudo divinitatis]], that is, perfect and true divinity with all its perfection. For in Christ the divine and human natures are united in one person. And it dwells in that nature [[2:9|corporeally|corporaliter]], that is, it is truly and immediately joined to His body, as also to His soul, not that it is itself a body. Moreover the divinity is said to be so united because the person of the Word, which is the divinity, is joined to the humanity.

paras.t: Deinceps ostendit Apostolus vanam esse rationem eorum qui per legis allegationem nitebantur Colossenses subvertere, inducendo eos ad cærimonialia legis. Et estis in illo, id est a Christo prout Deus est, et per ipsum prout est homo, Dei ac hominum mediator, repleti gratia et donis Spiritus Sancti, ita ut nequaquam indigeatis legalium observantia. Propterea scriptum est: De plenitudine ejus nos accepimus omnes gratiam pro gratia. Ipse quoque propter nos egenus factus est, ut ejus inopia divites essemus. Qui Christus, etiam secundum naturam assumptam, est caput, id est capitalis influxor, omnis principatus et potestatis, id est angelorum sanctorum: qui omnes a Christo homine purgantur, illuminantur ac perficiuntur, secundum Theologum.
paras.en: Next the Apostle shows the reasoning of those to be empty who were trying to subvert the Colossians by appeal to the law, leading them to the ceremonies of the law. [[2:10|And you are filled in him|Et estis in illo]], that is, by Christ as He is God, and through Him as He is man, the mediator of God and men[[1 Tim 2:5||]], [[2:10|filled|repleti]] with the grace and gifts of the Holy Ghost, so that you have no need at all of the observance of the legal ceremonies. Therefore it is written: [[John 1:16|And of his fulness we all have received: and grace for grace|De plenitudine ejus nos accepimus omnes gratiam pro gratia]]. He also became poor for our sakes, that through His poverty we might be rich[[2 Cor 8:9||]]. [[2:10|Who|Qui]], Christ, even according to the nature He assumed, [[2:10|is the head|est caput]], that is, the one who flows into them as head, [[2:10|of all principality and power|omnis principatus et potestatis]], that is, of the holy angels, who are all purified, enlightened and perfected by Christ as man, according to the Theologian [that is, Dionysius the Areopagite].

paras.t: In quo, id est cujus virtute, operatione et gratia, circumcisi estis circumcisione non manufacta, id est non carnali, legali ac litterali, in exspoliatione corporis carnis, id est amittendo particulam corporis quod est caro, videlicet pellem præputii quæ in illa circumcisione aufertur, sed in circumcisione Jesu Christi, id est, spirituali atque a Christo facta circumcisione circumcisi estis per expurgationem superfluitatis vitiorum ac passionum vestrarum. De qua circumcisione scriptum est: Circumcidimini Domino, et auferte præputia cordium vestrorum; et iterum alibi, Circumcidite præputium cordis vestri, et cervicem vestram ne induretis amplius.
paras.en: [[2:11|In whom|In quo]], that is, by whose power, working and grace, [[2:11|you are circumcised with circumcision not made by hand|circumcisi estis circumcisione non manufacta]], that is, not carnal, legal and literal, [[2:11|in despoiling of the body of the flesh|in exspoliatione corporis carnis]], that is, by losing a small part of the body that is flesh, namely the skin of the foreskin, which is removed in that circumcision; [[2:11|but in the circumcision of Christ|sed in circumcisione Jesu Christi]], that is, you are circumcised with a spiritual circumcision made by Christ, by the purging away of the excess of your vices and passions. Of this circumcision it is written: [[Jer 4:4|Be circumcised to the Lord, and take away the foreskins of your hearts|Circumcidimini Domino, et auferte præputia cordium vestrorum]]; and again elsewhere: [[Deut 10:16|Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and stiffen your neck no more|Circumcidite præputium cordis vestri, et cervicem vestram ne induretis amplius]].

paras.t: Consepulti ei, videlicet Christo, in Baptismo, id est in susceptione Baptismatis omnino vitiis mortificati, sicut et Christi corpus in sepulcro mortuum erat naturali vitæ. Vel hoc ideo dicitur, quoniam baptizati ter tinguntur in aqua, quemadmodum Christus triduo erat in monumento; et sicut Christus de sepulcro ad immortalem vitam surrexit, sic baptizati de sepulcro a vitiorum corruptione ac vetustate liberati ascendunt. Ideo subditur: in quo Christo et resurrexistis a ruina peccati, per fidem operationis Dei, id est per fidem quam Deus operatur seu creat in vobis: sine fide enim nemo spiritualiter surgit; qui Deus Pater vel Trinitas suscitavit illum a mortuis tertia die.
paras.en: [[2:12|Buried with him|Consepulti ei]], that is, with Christ, [[2:12|in baptism|in Baptismo]], that is, wholly dead to vices in receiving Baptism, as the body of Christ in the tomb was dead to natural life. Or this is said because the baptized are dipped three times in the water, as Christ was three days in the tomb; and as Christ rose from the tomb to immortal life, so the baptized come up from the tomb freed from the corruption and oldness of vices. Hence it is added: [[2:12|in whom also you are risen again|in quo et resurrexistis]], in Christ, from the fall of sin, [[2:12|by the faith of the operation of God|per fidem operationis Dei]], that is, by the faith which God works or creates in you: for without faith no one rises spiritually; [[2:12|who hath raised him up from the dead|qui suscitavit illum a mortuis]], that is, God the Father, or the Trinity, on the third day.

paras.t: Et vos quum mortui essetis spiritualiter, carentes vita gratiæ, in delictis, id est propter peccata vestra quibus naturalem legem reliquistis, et præputio carnis vestræ, id est propter carnalia vitia, vel propter originale peccatum quod per præputium traducitur, convivificavit cum illo, id est, ad vitam gratiæ suscitavit, quemadmodum Christum ad vitam naturalem humanam reduxit, suscitando eum a mortuis: vel, Convivificavit cum illo, id est, immortalitatem vobis jam dedit in spe, quam Christo dedit in re. Capitis namque præcessio, spes est membrorum. Donans, id est, gratis et sine merito vestro dimittens, vobis omnia delicta vestra merito Christi, dummodo tamen meritum illud vobis applicetur per fidem vel sacramenta Ecclesiæ.
paras.en: [[2:13|And you, when you were dead|Et vos quum mortui essetis]] spiritually, lacking the life of grace, [[2:13|in your sins|in delictis]], that is, through your sins by which you forsook the natural law, [[2:13|and the uncircumcision of your flesh|et præputio carnis vestræ]], that is, through carnal vices, or through original sin, which is handed down through the foreskin [that is, through carnal generation], [[2:13|he hath quickened together with him|convivificavit cum illo]], that is, raised you to the life of grace, as He brought Christ back to natural human life by raising Him from the dead; or, He hath quickened together with him, that is, He has already given you in hope the immortality He gave Christ in reality. For the going-before of the Head is the hope of the members. [[2:13|Forgiving|Donans]], that is, remitting freely and without your merit, [[2:13|you all offences|vobis omnia delicta]] of yours, by the merit of Christ, provided however that this merit be applied to you through faith or the sacraments of the Church.

paras.t: Delens ipse Christus, merito passionis suæ, quod adversum nos erat chirographum decreti, id est memoriale seu litteram humanæ transgressionis, qua homo protoplastus prævaricatus est in paradiso decretum, id est Dei præceptum. Hujus enim transgressionis memor fuit Deus ad puniendum, dæmon ad accusandum. Habuitque diabolus quasi litteram testimonialem reatus quem homo incurrit transgrediendo divinum præceptum, imo et tota posteritas primi parentis. Christus vero satisfaciendo pro peccatis nostris actualibus ac originalibus, eripuit totum genus humanum ab isto reatu, seu debito pœnæ pro peccato infligendæ. Et ita delevit prædictum chirographum, quod contra nos erat, quoniam erat testimonium faciens nos damnationi obnoxios. Quum vero peccatum dimittitur, dicimus Deum oblivisci illius. Dæmon quoque non potest de illo peccato accusationem efficacem obtendere. Quod chirographum erat contrarium nobis: sicut jam dictum est. Et ipsum tulit de medio, id est, ab universis hominibus abstulit illud chirographum, affigens illud cruci, id est, in sua passione illud occidens seu destruens, quantum in se erat. Eripuit enim nos de pœna pro peccato originali post hanc vitam infligenda, dummodo ei ut capiti uniamur per fidem et caritatem, quatenus virtus suæ passionis redundet in nos tanquam in membra ipsius.
paras.en: [[2:14|Blotting out|Delens]], Christ Himself, by the merit of His passion, [[2:14|the handwriting of the decree that was against us|quod adversum nos erat chirographum decreti]], that is, the record or written bond of human transgression, by which the first-formed man in paradise transgressed the decree[[Gen 3:6||]], that is, the commandment of God. For God kept this transgression in mind to punish it, the devil to accuse it. And the devil held, as it were, a written testimony of the guilt which man incurred by transgressing the divine commandment, and indeed the whole posterity of the first parent with him. But Christ, by making satisfaction for our actual and original sins, rescued the whole human race from this guilt, or debt of punishment to be inflicted for sin. And so He blotted out the said handwriting that was against us, since it was a testimony making us liable to damnation. Now when sin is forgiven, we say that God forgets it. Nor can the devil bring any effective accusation about that sin. [[2:14|Which was contrary to us|Quod erat contrarium nobis]], the handwriting, as has just been said. [[2:14|And he hath taken the same out of the way|Et ipsum tulit de medio]], that is, He took away that handwriting from all men, [[2:14|fastening it to the cross|affigens illud cruci]], that is, in His passion slaying or destroying it, as far as lay in Him. For He rescued us from the punishment to be inflicted after this life for original sin, provided we be united to Him as our head by faith and charity, so that the power of His passion may overflow into us as into His members.

paras.t: Et exspolians principatus et potestates, id est, dæmones superiores ac inferiores privans præda quam ceperant, puta animabus seu hominibus quos suo dominio subdiderant inducendo eos ad culpam. De hac exspoliatione ait ipse Salvator: Nunc princeps hujus mundi ejicietur foras: et item, Ego, inquit, si exaltatus fuero a terra, omnia traham ad me ipsum. Christus namque est qui domum adversarii nostri ingressus est, fortemque armatum alligavit, ac vasa ejus diripuit. Propter quod jubetur per Prophetam Christus vocari, Accelera, spolia detrahe, festina prædari. Traduxit confidenter, id est, prædam hanc dæmoni ablatam Christus securissime transtulit in regnum suum, præsidens eis quibus præsidebat diabolus. Nunc enim ponit eos in regno Ecclesiæ militantis, postea autem ponet eos (sicut jam plurimos posuit) in regno Ecclesiæ triumphantis. Palam triumphans, id est evidenter vincens, illos, id est diabolos, in semetipso, id est in proprii corporis crucifixione; vel, In semetipso, id est in propria persona ad inferos descendendo, et sanctos educendo, implens illud propheticum: De manu mortis liberabo eos, de morte redimam eos; ero mors tua, o mors, morsus tuus ero, inferne.
paras.en: [[2:15|And despoiling the principalities and powers|Et exspolians principatus et potestates]], that is, depriving the higher and lower demons of the prey they had taken, namely souls or men, whom they had brought under their dominion by leading them into sin. Of this despoiling the Saviour Himself says: [[John 12:31|now shall the prince of this world be cast out|Nunc princeps hujus mundi ejicietur foras]]; and again: [[John 12:32|And I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all things to myself|Ego, inquit, si exaltatus fuero a terra, omnia traham ad me ipsum]]. For it is Christ who entered the house of our adversary, bound the strong man armed, and plundered his goods[[Matt 12:29||]]. For this reason Christ is ordered by the Prophet to be called: Hasten to take away the spoils, make haste to take the prey[[Is 8:3||]] [the name *Maher-shalal-hash-baz* given in Isaias 8:3, which the Vulgate translates]. [[2:15|He hath exposed them confidently|Traduxit confidenter]], that is, Christ most securely carried this prey, taken from the devil, over into His kingdom, ruling over those whom the devil ruled. For now He places them in the kingdom of the Church militant, and later He will place them (as He has already placed very many) in the kingdom of the Church triumphant. [[2:15|In open shew, triumphing|Palam triumphans]], that is, manifestly conquering, [[2:15|over them|illos]], that is, the devils, [[2:15|in himself|in semetipso]], that is, in the crucifixion of His own body; or, In himself, that is, in His own person, by descending to hell and leading out the saints, fulfilling that prophecy: [[Osee 13:14|I will deliver them out of the hand of death. I will redeem them from death: O death, I will be thy death; O hell, I will be thy bite|De manu mortis liberabo eos, de morte redimam eos; ero mors tua, o mors, morsus tuus ero, inferne]].

paras.t: Ex his concludit Apostolus principale intentum, videlicet, quod non teneantur fideles ad observationem legalium post Christi passionem. Nemo ergo, id est, quum prædicta se ita habeant, nemo vos judicet, id est, damnabiles asserat, in cibo aut in potu, id est in usu victus, scilicet ob id quod non discernatis inter cibos more Judaico, aut in parte diei festi, id est ex parte omissionis Judaicarum celebritatum, videlicet aut neomeniæ, id est festi occurrentis in novilunio, aut sabbatorum, id est ultimorum dierum hebdomadæ; quæ omnia sunt umbra futurorum, id est obscura signa eorum quæ in novo Testamento geruntur: prout alibi dicit Apostolus, Umbram habens lex futurorum bonorum, non ipsam imaginem rerum; corpus autem Christi, id est, veritas per illa significata, per Christum impletur, ad eumque pertinet. Ideo Christi mysteriis consummatis, quando in cruce dicebat, Consummatum est, quando et velum templi scissum est, legalia cessaverunt, sicut figura cessat adveniente re figurata.
paras.en: From this the Apostle draws his principal point, namely that the faithful are not bound to observe the legal ceremonies after the passion of Christ. [[2:16|Let no man therefore|Nemo ergo]], that is, since the foregoing is so, let no man [[2:16|judge you|vos judicet]], that is, declare you worthy of condemnation, [[2:16|in meat or in drink|in cibo aut in potu]], that is, in the use of food, namely because you do not distinguish between foods in the Jewish manner, [[2:16|or in respect of a festival day|aut in parte diei festi]], that is, on account of omitting the Jewish solemnities, namely [[2:16|or of the new moon|aut neomeniæ]], that is, the feast falling at the new moon, [[2:16|or of the sabbaths|aut sabbatorum]], that is, of the last days of the week; [[2:17|which|quæ]] all [[2:17|are a shadow of things to come|sunt umbra futurorum]], that is, obscure signs of what is accomplished in the New Testament: as the Apostle says elsewhere: [[Heb 10:1|For the law, having a shadow of the good things to come, not the very image of the things|Umbram habens lex futurorum bonorum, non ipsam imaginem rerum]]; [[2:17|but the body is of Christ|corpus autem Christi]], that is, the truth signified by them is fulfilled through Christ and belongs to Him. Therefore, when the mysteries of Christ were accomplished, when He said on the cross, [[John 19:30|It is consummated|Consummatum est]], when also the veil of the temple was rent[[Matt 27:51||]], the legal ceremonies ceased, as the figure ceases when the thing figured arrives.

paras.t: Præterea agit Apostolus contra eos qui per simulatam sanctitatem nitebantur subvertere Colossenses. Nemo vos seducat, volens, id est suadere contendens, in humilitate et religione angelorum, id est per fictam humilitatem et apparentem religionem, quibus angelis similis videtur, tanquam verus nuntius Dei, sicut et angelus, quæ non vidit, id est observationes legalium quæ non intellexit secundum spiritualem et mysticam rationem, videlicet prout sunt signa futuri: hoc est, cupiens probare hac circumventione legalia esse servanda: qui est ambulans frustra, id est infructuose laborans, inflatus sensu carnis suæ, id est tumidus et superbus intellectu carnali, carnaliter intelligente legalia, et sensualitatem ac imaginationem potius quam spiritualem rationem sequente, sapiens in oculis propriis; et non tenens caput, id est Christo non inhærens, ex quo totum corpus, id est universa Ecclesia, per nexus fidei et conjunctiones sanctæ dilectionis subministratum, id est exhibitum, vel sibi invicem subserviens, et constructum, id est in unum redactum, hoc est spiritualiter copulatum per fidem, spem, caritatem, et opera atque obsequia pia, quibus uniuntur et unum mysticum corpus efficiuntur fideles: quod corpus hoc modo compactum, crescit in augmentum Dei, id est in magnitudinem spiritualem, videlicet in incrementum virtutum per gratiam et efficientiam Dei.
paras.en: Further, the Apostle deals with those who were trying to subvert the Colossians by feigned holiness. [[2:18|Let no man seduce you, willing|Nemo vos seducat, volens]], that is, striving to persuade, [[2:18|in humility and religion of angels|in humilitate et religione angelorum]], that is, by feigned humility and apparent religion, by which he seems like the angels, as if he were a true messenger of God, as an angel is; [[2:18|the things which he hath not seen|quæ non vidit]], that is, the legal observances, which he has not understood according to their spiritual and mystical meaning, namely as signs of what was to come: that is, wishing by this trickery to prove that the legal ceremonies must be kept; who is [[2:18|walking in the things which he hath not seen, in vain|ambulans frustra]], that is, labouring fruitlessly, [[2:18|puffed up by the sense of his flesh|inflatus sensu carnis suæ]], that is, swollen and proud with a carnal understanding, which understands the legal ceremonies carnally and follows sensuality and imagination rather than spiritual reason, wise in his own eyes[[Is 5:21||]]; [[2:19|And not holding the head|et non tenens caput]], that is, not clinging to Christ, [[2:19|from which the whole body|ex quo totum corpus]], that is, the whole Church, [[2:19|by joints|per nexus]] of faith [[2:19|and bands|et conjunctiones]] of holy love, [[2:19|being supplied with nourishment|subministratum]], that is, furnished, or serving one another, [[2:19|and compacted|et constructum]], that is, brought into one, that is, spiritually joined by faith, hope, charity, and good works and services, by which the faithful are united and made one mystical body[[Rom 12:5||]]: which body, thus compacted, [[2:19|groweth into the increase of God|crescit in augmentum Dei]], that is, into spiritual greatness, namely into the increase of the virtues by the grace and working of God.

paras.t: Si ergo mortui estis cum Christo, id est a vitiis mortificati ac purificati, sicut et Christus semper a vitiis immunissimus fuit: mortui, inquam, ab elementis hujus mundi, id est ab inordinato affectu et cultu sensibilium ac sæcularium rerum; vel, Mortui cum Christo, id est, si Christo adhærentes, separati estis ab elementis hujus mundi, id est a lege, ejusque cærimonialibus præceptis, in quibus est institutio puerorum, mundana quærentium. In lege namque quasi in elementis alphabeti, est litteralis ac puerilis institutio. Quid adhuc, id est usque in præsens, videlicet evangelica veritate jam patefacta, tanquam viventes in mundo, id est quasi sæcularem vitam ducentes, non Deo viventes, decernitis, id est, determinatis legalia esse servanda? dicentes ad invicem: Ne tetigeritis, neque gustaveritis, neque contrectaveritis ea quæ lex prohibet tangi, gustari aut contrectari.
paras.en: [[2:20|If then you be dead with Christ|Si ergo mortui estis cum Christo]], that is, mortified and purified from vices, as Christ was ever wholly free from vices: dead, I say, [[2:20|from the elements of this world|ab elementis hujus mundi]], that is, from inordinate affection for and devotion to sensible and worldly things; or, Dead with Christ, that is, if, cleaving to Christ, you are separated from the elements of this world, that is, from the law and its ceremonial precepts, in which lies the schooling of children who seek worldly things. For in the law, as in the elements [that is, the letters] of the alphabet, there is a literal and childish schooling. [[2:20|Why do you yet|quid adhuc]], that is, up to the present, namely now that the gospel truth has been revealed, [[2:20|as though living in the world|tanquam viventes in mundo]], that is, as leading a worldly life, not living to God, [[2:20|decree|decernitis]], that is, determine that the legal ceremonies must be kept? saying to one another: [[2:21|Touch not: taste not: handle not.|Ne tetigeritis, neque gustaveritis, neque contrectaveritis:]] the things which the law forbids to be touched, tasted or handled.

paras.t: Quæ sunt omnia in interitum, id est, ista decernere, seu legalia observare, mortem spiritualem inducunt, ipso usu, id est per hoc quod Judaico ritu servantur, secundum præcepta et doctrinas hominum, id est, prout a Pharisæis et Scribis jubentur et persuadentur servari post Christi passionem. Quamvis enim præcepta cærimonialia fuerint divinitus data, et suo tempore observanda, tamen ut observentur tempore novæ legis non est secundum præceptum doctrinamque Dei, sed hominum Judæorum.
paras.en: [[2:22|Which all are unto destruction|Quæ sunt omnia in interitum]], that is, to decree these things, or to observe the legal ceremonies, brings on spiritual death, [[2:22|by the very use|ipso usu]], that is, by their being kept in the Jewish rite, [[2:22|according to the precepts and doctrines of men|secundum præcepta et doctrinas hominum]], that is, as they are commanded and urged to be kept after Christ's passion by the Pharisees and Scribes. For although the ceremonial precepts were given by God and were to be observed in their own time, yet that they should be observed in the time of the new law is not according to the precept and doctrine of God, but of men, the Jews.

paras.t: Quæ præcepta, tempore gratiæ, sunt rationem quidem habentia sapientiæ, id est, speciem sapientiæ habent, non essentiam: habentque apparentiam seu speciem hanc in superstitione, quia videntur ad superexcedentem religionem pertinere, et humilitate simulata, quoniam observatores eorum humilitatem confingunt, et Deo obedire se simulant; et quia sunt non ad parcendum corpori, quoniam observatio legalium laboriosissima est, sicque videtur pertinere ad rigorem justitiæ, non ad carnalitatem; ideo etiam, quia sunt non in honore aliquo, id est, humanum honorem non quærunt observatores eorum, permittentes carnem præputii sui circumcidi; et quia non sunt ad saturitatem carnis, id est, etiam ideo speciem sapientiæ habent legalia hæc, quoniam multa delectabilia subtrahunt corpori, ut carnes porcinas: unde videntur ad sobrietatem et abstinentiam pertinere: propter quod observatores eorum, judicant non observantes esse gulosos.
paras.en: [[2:23|Which things|Quæ]] precepts, in the time of grace, [[2:23|have indeed a shew of wisdom|sunt rationem quidem habentia sapientiæ]], that is, they have the appearance of wisdom, not its substance: and they have this appearance or show [[2:23|in superstition|in superstitione]], because they seem to belong to an exceeding religion, [[2:23|and humility|et humilitate]] feigned, since those who observe them make a show of humility and pretend to obey God; [[2:23|and|et]] because they are [[2:23|not sparing the body|non ad parcendum corpori]], since the observance of the legal ceremonies is most laborious, and so seems to belong to the rigour of justice, not to carnality; and also because they are [[2:23|not in any honour|non in honore aliquo]], that is, those who observe them do not seek human honour, allowing the flesh of their foreskin to be circumcised; and because they are not [[2:23|to the filling of the flesh|ad saturitatem carnis]], that is, these legal ceremonies have the appearance of wisdom also because they withdraw many pleasant things from the body, such as pork: hence they seem to belong to sobriety and abstinence; for which reason those who observe them judge those who do not to be gluttons.
